gloss: Literally 'at first sight like old friends'; figuratively means to feel an instant connection.
teaser: Ever met someone and felt like you've known them forever? This idiom captures that feeling.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever met someone and felt like you've known them forever? This idiom captures that feeling.[break 1s]The phrase is: 一见如故, yī jiàn rú gù.[break 0.5s]一 (yī) - one, [break 0.5s]见 (jiàn) - see, [break 0.5s]如 (rú) - like, [break 0.5s]故 (gù) - old friend.[break 1s]So, 一见如故 means 'at first sight like old friends', which conveys that instant connection or familiarity.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]This idiom dates back to the Tang Dynasty, where it was said that two people who met for the first time felt as if they had been friends for years. It highlighted the warmth and ease in their interaction, symbolizing that some connections are simply meant to be. The phrase has since been used to describe those serendipitous encounters that leave a lasting impression.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 他们第一次见面就一见如故。[break 1s]They felt like old friends when they met for the first time.[break 1s]Example 2: 我和她一见如故，聊了很久。[break 1s]She and I hit it off right away and talked for a long time.[break 1s]Example 3: 这两位艺术家在展览上相遇，立刻一见如故。[break 1s]The two artists met at the exhibition and instantly felt like old friends.[break 1s]So, 一见如故 means to feel an instant connection. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
